finding.source: Request value bound to the @inspectFile target (e.g. REQUEST_BODY); attacker controls bytes and size.
finding.sink: exec.CommandContext(ctx, o.path, value) at line 53; verdict at lines 54-58.

finding.guards_checked: 10s timeout only bounds time and fails open. No shell used, so no shell injection. No '--' separator (see F3). Repro not executed; Go NUL/E2BIG behavior is from stdlib knowledge and needs a unit test to confirm.

finding.claim: When url.ParseRequestURI fails, ExtractGetArguments is skipped and QUERY_STRING is set empty, so the query string (ARGS_GET, QUERY_STRING) is uninspected. Known bug per the test comment.
finding.source: Raw request target, e.g. GET /%zz?id=<payload> (invalid percent-escape in path, control bytes, or target not starting with '/').
finding.sink: ARGS_GET / ARGS / QUERY_STRING inspection (ExtractGetArguments skipped; queryString set to empty).

trace.note: url.ParseRequestURI fails on invalid path escape, control bytes, or non-slash-leading target
error branch: sets URLENCODED_ERROR, REQUEST_URI, path = uri
fallback query extraction is commented out (lines 840-851)
ExtractGetArguments only reached on success branch; never called here

finding.guards_checked: URLENCODED_ERROR is set but the engine does not deny on it by itself. Rules matching raw REQUEST_URI/REQUEST_LINE still see the bytes, so bypass is limited to ARGS/QUERY_STRING-specific rules. transaction_test.go:2416-2419 pins this as a known bug. Exploitability depends on backend accepting the malformed target; Go net/http rejects some of these with 400 before the WAF, so risk is mainly behind non-Go connectors.
